title: Return Ward · Recovery cradle
summary:
**Direction declined, 10 November 2026.** The player frame felt too bulky, the flesh on its back looked out of place, and the recovery cradle did not fit the intended aesthetic. The next round starts with the player silhouette.

**Original lore · provisional**

At the end of a sortie, the pilot wakes up in the hangar. Usually, the recovery crew brings the mech home too. For decades, crews have been writing off frames they couldn’t reach. Now some of those frames are walking home. One has worn a circular path around a demolished apartment block. Every time it reaches where the front door stood, it stops and lifts its hand.

**The first enemy I’d draw** is a recovery cradle walking on two enormous human forearms. It used to carry disabled mechs back to the ward. Now it tries to collect active ones. At a distance you hear its fingertips drumming on concrete. Before it lunges, both palms settle flat and the drumming stops. A sideways boost lets it sail past with the empty cradle open.

**The roguelite hook** is that a failed run can leave a body in the district. On a later sortie, you might hear your old left-hand weapon firing its familiar rhythm somewhere below you. Hunting the frame could recover that weapon. Following it quietly could reveal where the abandoned bodies go.

items.title: The intake yard
items.alt: A green player mech seen from behind carries a cleaver, drum gun, shoulder launcher and upright cannon. Across the yard, an empty hospital cradle braces on two giant human hands.
items.body:
**Player frame.** The cleaver and drum gun occupy the hands. The launcher and slim cannon sit outside the shoulders, leaving the pale shoulder blades visible through a dark membrane. This four-weapon loadout explores how much of the body the player could see from the chase camera.

**Recovery cradle.** Its padded seat faces the player, with loose restraints ready for a passenger. Its fingertips tap as it approaches. When both palms plant flat and the tapping stops, the cradle is about to lunge. The painting shows that held pose.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/return-ward/intake-yard-v001.png)
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Paint one landscape game concept keyframe titled in spirit "The Return Ward", without text. An unmistakable still moment of biomechanical horror from a third-person mech action game. A heavily loaded pilot mech, viewed from behind on the LEFT, comes upon a former hospital recovery machine across a deserted ambulance intake court on the RIGHT. Show their whole silhouettes and a strip of empty concrete between them. The player is about eight metres tall. The cradle in the middle distance is close enough for both of its planted hands to read instantly. Camera a little above the player's shoulder joints, looking slightly downward, near-rear three-quarter; a cinematic 3:2 horizontal composition, both subjects in crisp focus, separated against pale concrete. Give the cradle at least a third of the frame. Both its hands should be well inside the canvas.
PLAYER: Compact blunt, slab-sided industrial cockpit with a small sealed head or sensor turret, low center of gravity, heavy mechanical legs on articulated work boots, two long forearms ending in ordinary segmented mechanical grippers with broad wrists. A solid work machine. Color identity: flaking petrol-green enamel over dark steel, small areas of yellowed hospital white, rust dust. The player's exposed central upper back is the intimate detail: two large pale scapula shapes pressing up against a taut, smoky translucent rubber bellows on either side of a central seam; one scapula is slightly hitched. Keep this central patch CLEAR and visible between the outboard equipment. It ought to feel like something involuntarily shrugging within the housing. Minimal other anatomy on the player. Use broad distinctive masses, restrained little hardware marks at service seams.
LOADOUT: Show exactly FOUR different detachable, stylized fictional game weapons in clean separated silhouettes, one gripped in each hand and one mounted on each of two rigid outboard dorsal rails. From the rear view: high left, a squat rectangular cluster launcher with a honeycomb of dark cells; high right, a single slender upright ivory pulse cannon. Keep the two shoulders and the space between them open. Low left, a cleaver-shaped field blade gripped in the left hand and pointing down and OUT to the left with clear ground behind it; low right, a chunky short drum-shaped pulse gun gripped in the right hand, right forearm slightly out to the side. Each of the four silhouettes visible at the same time, all inactive, slight outward angles to prevent overlaps; no more turrets or blade-like antennae. A three-quarter glimpse of the weapon bodies is enough.
ENEMY: An empty adult-mech-sized rescue cradle, a faded cream U-shaped hospital transport shell tilted open TOWARD THE VIEWER, with a nearly vertical padded litter inside, broad old lap restraints hanging loose, and a signal lamp. Where the wheels would be, it is supported entirely by exactly TWO colossal uncannily human-looking forearms and human hands. The shell connects at the elbows and hangs low BETWEEN the arms. Long scarless, pallid, weight-bearing forearms, worn gray at their heavily callused fingertips and wrists, trembling under its weight. Both enormous palms are FLAT DOWN on the ground and every finger is splayed under load, elbows flexed, empty cradle poised to surge forward. This enemy has no legs, no head, no gun, no wheels. The suggestion of an old rescue apparatus asking to pick up the player should feel more disturbing than a monster roar. No people, gore, wounds or injured occupants.
SETTING AND FINISH: A neglected concrete intake yard, tall banded ward windows and one closed ambulance bay, obsolete flaking lane stripes leading between the two machines, unlit faded stop lamp. Flat winter daylight breaking in from one side, pale concrete floor makes hands and player weapons read; warm raking light on the palms, cool oxidized steel and desaturated celadon. Sparse background. Beautiful painterly industrial concept art with big graphic masses, precise joints, worn material transitions and fine gouache brushwork. A tense held breath before the lunge. No graphic overlays, no lettering, no captions, no UI, no panel layout.
